items.followUp: How did Rutherford discover the proton?

rubric.why: Identifies the experiment that produced the radiation.
rubric.description: Chadwick bombarded beryllium with alpha particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming beryllium and alpha particles (or helium nuclei).

rubric.why: Shows how the experiment led to the identification of the neutron.
rubric.description: The radiation was neutral and knocked protons out of paraffin wax; Chadwick concluded it consisted of neutrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the radiation as neutral/neutrons or describing its effect on paraffin wax.

modelAnswer: Chadwick bombarded beryllium with alpha particles, producing a highly penetrating radiation.
The radiation was neutral and knocked protons out of paraffin wax; Chadwick concluded that it consisted of neutrons.

rubric.why: States that electronegativity is an attracting tendency.
rubric.description: Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom to attract electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the idea of attraction by an atom.

rubric.description: The atom attracts the shared pair of electrons in a covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying the shared or bonding electrons.

modelAnswer: Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself in a covalent bond.

items.followUp: How does metallic character change across a period and down a group?

rubric.why: Checks the trend down a group.
rubric.description: Atomic radius increases from top to bottom in a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atomic radius increases down a group.

rubric.why: Checks the trend across a period.
rubric.description: Atomic radius decreases from left to right across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atomic radius decreases across a period.

modelAnswer: Atomic radius increases from top to bottom in a group.
Atomic radius decreases from left to right across a period.

items.followUp: Explain why atomic radius decreases from left to right across a period.

rubric.why: Identifies the increasing attraction of the nucleus across a period.
rubric.description: Ionization energy increases across a period because nuclear charge increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the trend to increasing nuclear charge or attraction.

rubric.why: Explains why electrons are easier to remove farther down a group.
rubric.description: Ionization energy decreases down a group because the outer electron is farther from the nucleus and shielding increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the decrease to greater distance, larger atomic radius, or increased shielding.

modelAnswer: Across a period, nuclear charge increases while atomic radius decreases, so the outer electron is attracted more strongly and more energy is needed to remove it.
Down a group, atomic radius and shielding increase, so the outer electron is less strongly attracted and less energy is needed to remove it.

items.followUp: What is meant by a non-polar covalent bond?

rubric.why: Distinguishes a polar bond by unequal sharing.
rubric.description: A polar covalent bond involves unequal sharing of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the bonding electrons are shared unequally.

rubric.why: Identifies the cause or resulting partial charges of the polarity.
rubric.description: The unequal sharing results from a difference in electronegativity and produces partial charges.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning an electronegativity difference or partial charges.

modelAnswer: A polar covalent bond is a covalent bond in which the bonded atoms share the electron pair unequally because of a difference in electronegativity.
This unequal sharing produces partial positive and partial negative charges on the atoms.

items.followUp: Write two properties of ionic compounds.

rubric.why: Assesses a characteristic physical property of covalent compounds.
rubric.description: Covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating low melting point or low boiling point.

rubric.description: Covalent compounds generally do not conduct electricity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they do not conduct, or are poor conductors of, electricity.

modelAnswer: Covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points.
They generally do not conduct electricity.

items.followUp: Why do solids have a definite shape and volume?

rubric.why: Identifies the arrangement of particles in a solid.
rubric.description: Particles in a solid are closely packed in fixed positions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that solid particles are closely packed or fixed in position.

rubric.why: Explains why the particles cannot move freely and the solid remains rigid.
rubric.description: Strong forces hold the particles in place; they can only vibrate about their fixed positions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking strong forces or restricted particle motion to rigidity.

modelAnswer: Particles in a solid are closely packed and held in fixed positions by strong forces of attraction.
They can only vibrate about these positions and cannot move freely, so the solid is rigid.

rubric.why: Identifies the change of state involved.
rubric.description: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that liquid changes into vapour or gas.

rubric.description: Evaporation occurs at the surface of a liquid and can occur below its boiling point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the surface or that it occurs below the boiling point.

modelAnswer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface.
It can occur at temperatures below the boiling point of the liquid.
